items.title: Evacuations as death toll rises to 53 after Russian airstrike on Komyshuvakha
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:

items.title: Pope Leo XIV opens his South America tour in Uruguay
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
<article>Pope Leo XIV Friday opened a South American tour in Uruguay, a country with deep secular roots. The Vatican estimated 30,000 people turned out along his route and at the ceremony. Crowds welcomed the pontiff as he rode through Montevideo in his popemobile before joining President Yamandú Orsi for a formal reception.
 (AP Video by: Silvia Stellacci, Martín Silva Rey and Luciano Paglia; Production by Paolo Santalucia)

items.title: Dad of co-pilot in Florida Learjet crash says she fought until the 'last minute'
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
<article>The father of the 20-year-old co-pilot who died along with eight others when their Learjet crashed in Florida said Friday he has listened to his daughter’s final radio transmissions “many times” since the crash.

Allan Filgueiras, himself a pilot, was searching for answers as to why the plane plunged from the sky on Sunday — but what he found was pride in how his daughter, Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, handled the crisis.</article>

items.title: Democratic wins by clergy show strength of a religious left
items.author: Associated Press
items.content: <article>Clergy and other Democratic candidates with an unapologetically Christian message to “love your neighbor” helped their party flip control of Congress, highlighting the religious left's strength as a counter to evangelical support for President Donald Trump.</article>

items.title: Colorado family loses home to floods, unsure how to rebuild
items.author: Associated Press
items.content: <article>Matthew Martinez has lived nearly all of his 60 years on a piece of property on the Navajo River and not once saw severe flooding until now. In just two weeks, the Navajo River has surged twice through his home and outbuildings in far southwestern Colorado.</article>

items.title: Why there's still no new government in Israel
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
<article>Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc of parties, led by his own Likud party, won 53 seats, with his main opposition winning 48 seats, and Arab-led parties securing the other 19. This means that any government will be a coalition of parties. Meanwhile, Netanyahu remains as caretaker Prime Minister. (Produced by Luke Garratt)
